summary: array-flatten-utils ships a native-addon dropper that decrypts and executes an opaque bundled payload on require
details: The package is advertised as a trivial array-flattening utility (index.js is ~652 bytes) but ships three platform-specific native addons (native_win.node, native_mac.node, native.napi.node) and a 1.34 MB opaque high-entropy blob named.napi_cache at the package root. index.js unconditionally requires the platform-matching.node addon, so the addon code runs on any require() of the package. The addons do not implement array utilities; embedded strings show they read.napi_cache, stage it to disk, and execute it: on Windows, writing %s.nc%lu.js and spawning it with `node "%s"`; on POSIX, writing /tmp/.%u, chmod, then fork/setsid/execlp. Before executing, the addons perform sandbox, CI, and debugger evasion: they check environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SANDBOX, NETLIFY, VERCEL), inspect /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/self/status for TracerPid, and /proc/self/maps on Linux, and on Windows enumerate processes for wireshark, procmon, procexp, x64dbg, ollydbg, fiddler, httpdebug and call IsDebuggerPresent / CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, suppressing the payload inside analysis environments and executing only on real developer machines. The combination of a cover-story name, an opaque encrypted second-stage blob, a native loader, require-time execution, and dedicated analysis-evasion is a dropper that runs attacker-controlled code on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
